question: What conflicting experiences do maintainers and users report about running Bun in production, and which concrete compatibility or reliability claims can be traced to evidence rather than opinion?

claims.text: Bun's own compatibility docs also document remaining gaps, including partial `node:async_hooks`, partial `node:child_process`, and `node:cluster` being implemented but not battle-tested.

rejected_claims.text: Bun is universally production-safe for Node.js workloads.
rejected_claims.reason: Overly broad; the supplied evidence shows documented gaps and multiple production bug reports.

rejected_claims.text: Virtually any Node.js app works on Bun.
rejected_claims.reason: This is a maintainer marketing claim in the supplied evidence, but not independently established by the cited compatibility and issue evidence.

rejected_claims.text: Bun is broadly unreliable in production.
rejected_claims.reason: Unsupported as a general statement; the evidence proves specific failures existed, not prevalence across all production users.

rejected_claims.text: AsyncLocalStorage performance on Bun blocks production OpenTelemetry.
rejected_claims.reason: Time-unstable/contradictory in the supplied evidence because the cited issue was later updated to say the reported production problem did not exist in release builds.

rejected_claims.text: Bun maintainers publicly said Bun 1.0 was "stable and production-ready," so a production-readiness claim from maintainers is directly evidenced.
rejected_claims.reason: required concept is absent from teacher-run evidence: maintainer_claim

rejected_claims.text: Concrete compatibility evidence exists in Bun's published test results: Bun 1.4 said several Node modules passed 97% of Node's tests, `node:quic` passed 99%, and some modules passed 100%.
rejected_claims.reason: claim text is not lexically grounded in teacher-run evidence

rejected_claims.text: For native addons, the evidence is mixed rather than absolute: Bun's tracker says all `napi_*` and `node_api_*` functions were implemented, but the reported combined Node-API status was 74 pass / 23 todo / 76.3% on Linux.
rejected_claims.reason: required concept is absent from teacher-run evidence: partial_parity

rejected_claims.text: Users and platform operators report some successful production use: one discussion participant said they had used Bun in production since April 2023 on Heroku, and Vercel launched Bun runtime support in public beta while recommending Node.js for maximum compatibility.
rejected_claims.reason: required concept is absent from teacher-run evidence: positive_reports

rejected_claims.text: Users also report concrete production problems, including memory growth or crashes, production-mode-only failures, and `bun install --production` problems; Bun later said one workspace `--production` devDependency bug was fixed.
rejected_claims.reason: claim text is not lexically grounded in teacher-run evidence
